scope.description: One fault-free execution of a normally bootstrapped three-node in-memory cluster with heartbeat, election and leader-lease timeouts all set to 300ms: a control VerifyLeader on the healthy leader, then isolation of the leader from both followers and a second VerifyLeader measured against a 6s client-side wait limit.
assumptions: MakeCluster(3) performs real bootstrap, election and heartbeats through the in-memory transport, and c.Partition isolates the leader while leaving the other two connected to each other.
LeaderLeaseTimeout must not exceed HeartbeatTimeout, so all three timeouts are set to 300ms and the expected completion bound is a small multiple of that value.
The client-side wait limit of 6s is generous relative to the 300ms lease, so remaining unanswered past it would be a hang rather than an expected bound.
The leader is still in the Leader state when the isolated call is issued, so the measured path is the lease check and the step-down cleanup rather than a non-leader rejection.
excluded: Configurations with other lease, heartbeat or election ratios (for example a lease far below the heartbeat timeout).
Crash and restart scenarios, and any network transport behaviour.
The followers' own election while the leader is isolated.

basis.prefix: Built with captured test facilities and real producers only: MakeCluster(3, conf) with HeartbeatTimeout, ElectionTimeout and LeaderLeaseTimeout all 300ms bootstraps the cluster and c.Leader() returns the leader; the harness emits verify_control_start with the node identity, its state and the lease, calls VerifyLeader and emits verify_healthy with the error, elapsed time and state. It then isolates the leader from its peers with c.Partition, emits verify_probe_start with the node identity, state, lease and connected-peer count, issues VerifyLeader again, waits on the returned future from a separate goroutine against a 6s limit, and emits verify_partitioned with completion, elapsed time, error text, state and the wait limit. No storage is pre-filled and no production code is modified.
basis.requirement: VerifyLeader issued by a leader that cannot contact a quorum completes within a bound set by the leader lease and reports an error instead of hanging or claiming success, while the same call on a healthy leader succeeds immediately.
basis.responsibility: Verification completion for a stranded leader: the leader loop's lease check that ends leadership, the step-down cleanup that answers pending verifications, and the verification path that counts only peer replies.

comparisons.description: Control: on a healthy cluster the leader's verification succeeds, so the probe measures a working path before the isolation.
Bounded completion: the isolated leader's verification returns within the client wait limit instead of hanging on peers that cannot answer.
Correctness of the endpoint: the stranded verification fails rather than reporting success, because leadership ended.
